title: Cohomology over opens sheafifies to the cohomology sheaf
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and let $D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the derived category of the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. As in [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], choose functorially in the complex $K$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules a K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $H^q(U,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be the functor with $H^q(U,K)=H^q(\Gamma(U,I(K)))$ and $H^q(U,f)=H^q(\Gamma(U,I(f)))$ for a morphism of complexes $f$; it is well defined on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ by the argument of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], since $\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive and carries homotopies to homotopies, and for $V\subseteq U$ restriction of sections of $I(K)$ gives restriction maps $H^q(U,K)\to H^q(V,K)$. Then for every object $K$ of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $q$, the presheaf $U\mapsto H^q(U,K)$ has sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] canonically isomorphic to the cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$, naturally in $K$. Consequently, every element of the stalk $H^q(K)_x$ is the germ of some section in $H^q(U,K)$ for an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a section whose germ is zero becomes zero after restricting to a smaller neighborhood of $x$, and for a morphism $f:K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $s\in H^q(U,K)$ the germ of $H^q(U,f)(s)$ at $x\in U$ is $H^q(f)_x(s_x)$.

proof.text: Naturality of the quasi-isomorphism K to I(K), and two-out-of-three, show that I sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence. The additive underlying-presheaf functor preserves homotopies; homology factors through the homotopy category, so the resolved presheaf cohomology functor R inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Localization.lift constructs P with Localization.fac giving Q followed by P isomorphic to R.

Use abelian, rather than module, sheafification. It is exact. The underlying-abelian-sheaf functor T is exact by Mathlib finite-limit preservation and the proved source-library instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf. For U the sheaf inclusion and S abelian sheafification, the invertible counit gives (T followed by U) followed by S isomorphic to T. Apply the natural homology comparison for exact functors first to S and then T, and apply the counit termwise. This gives the private complexSheafificationHomologyIso for every complex, naturally in chain maps.

The natural resolution map induces an isomorphism on homology. Compose its inverse with the preceding complex-level comparison and DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors to identify R followed by sheafification with Q followed by derived homology followed by T. Localization.liftNatIso descends this natural isomorphism to e on the derived category. Define theta to be the sheafification unit followed by the underlying-presheaf map of e.

The stalk map of theta is a composite of isomorphisms: the sheafification-unit stalk map and the stalk map of e. Its surjectivity and TopCat.Presheaf.exists_germ_eq give a local representative for every target stalk element. Its injectivity reduces a zero image germ to a zero source germ; TopCat.Presheaf.germ_eq compares the section with zero and produces the smaller neighborhood. These are the underlying abelian-group clauses of the stalk description, with no bundled module-stalk functor required. Finally, apply TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply and the open-component of theta.naturality to obtain the morphism compatibility.
